payload.title: Available Ball Box
payload.summary: Players keep the ball available inside a square while a passive defender shadows and the coach calls surface changes.
payload.description: A lightly opposed technical box where one player maintains playable distance from the ball while a shadow defender follows without tackling. The active player must switch surfaces on command and glance up every three touches.

field.guidance: One 10-yard square per pair; add squares for larger groups.

objectives: Keep the ball within one stride under a passive shadow.
Change surface on command without trapping the ball.
Glance up every three touches to notice when the ball is free.
setupInstructions: Mark a 10-yard square with four cones.
Pair players: one ball carrier, one passive shadow.
Shadow follows at arm's length without tackling for the first round.
Coach stands outside and calls surface changes.
organization: Work 45-second rounds then swap roles.
Use multiple squares if numbers exceed six pairs.
Progress to active jockeying only after three clean rounds.
howItWorks: The carrier moves anywhere in the box keeping the ball available.
The shadow mirrors movement without winning the ball initially.
Every three touches the carrier glances up and calls free or tight.
On coach command the carrier switches surface immediately.
Partners swap after each round.
resetInstructions: If the ball leaves the box, the carrier retrieves it and restarts from the center.
Rotate waiting players into shadow roles to balance uneven numbers.
coachingPoints: Available means close — not glued to the foot.
Use the sole to escape a tight moment, then push away.
Glance up on the step after contact, not during it.
Shadow stays honest — no tackles until the coach upgrades pressure.

commonMistakes.mistake: Carrier stops on the ball when shadow closes.
commonMistakes.correction: Sole settle and push to the far foot in one motion.

commonMistakes.mistake: Shadow tackles too early.
commonMistakes.correction: Shadow keeps hands behind back and mirrors only.

commonMistakes.mistake: Carrier never looks up.
commonMistakes.correction: Require a verbal free or tight call every three touches.

progressions.title: Active jockey
progressions.description: Shadow can poke the ball after the carrier looks up twice.

progressions.title: Smaller box
progressions.description: Shrink to eight yards to increase pressure.

regressions.title: No shadow
regressions.description: Solo work with coach calling surfaces from outside.

regressions.title: Larger box
regressions.description: Expand to 12 yards and walk before jogging.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Trios rotate shadow role; waiting player calls surface changes.

steps.title: Mark the square
steps.explanation: Carrier and shadow begin in the center of a 10-yard box.
steps.playerAction: Carrier identifies box edges and shadow role.

steps.title: Move with the shadow
steps.explanation: The carrier dribbles while the shadow mirrors at arm's length.
steps.playerAction: Carrier keeps ball within one stride.

steps.title: Surface change on command
steps.explanation: Coach calls outside; carrier shifts to the far foot without stopping.
steps.playerAction: Carrier changes foot immediately.

steps.title: Call free or tight, then rotate
steps.explanation: After three touches the carrier glances up, announces whether the ball is free, and roles rotate.
steps.playerAction: Carrier scans and calls free or tight.
steps.ballAction: Ball remains playable during the scan.
steps.coachingPurpose: Build the transition habit of noticing ball state.

safetyNotes: Shadow players keep hands behind back in passive rounds.
No tackling until coach announces active jockeying.

payload.title: Open-Body Receiving Diamond
payload.summary: Players check away, receive across the body, and choose the next side of a passing diamond.
payload.description: A repeatable passing pattern that develops the timing and mechanics of arriving side-on. Players check away, receive on the far foot, prepare the next pass with the first touch, and follow their pass around the diamond.

field.guidance: Build one 12-to-15-yard diamond per group of four to six.

objectives: Check away and arrive as the passer looks up.
Receive on a half-turn with the next cone visible.
Use the first touch to prepare the next pass.
setupInstructions: Place four cones in a 12-to-15-yard diamond.
Put one player at each cone; extra players queue behind the starting cone.
Start one ball at the top cone.
Pass clockwise, then reverse direction between rounds.
organization: Use groups of four to six with one active ball per diamond.
Players follow their pass to preserve one player at each cone.
Run in both directions so players receive with both feet.
howItWorks: The next receiver checks away from the cone and returns side-on.
The passer plays to the receiver's safe far foot.
The receiver takes the first touch across the body toward the next cone.
The receiver passes to the next player while the original passer follows the pass.
resetInstructions: A loose ball is recovered by the nearest player while everyone holds the next open cone.
Restart from the nearest occupied cone rather than returning to the beginning.
coachingPoints: Check away early enough to arrive, not wait.
See the passer and next cone in the same body shape.
Receive with the far foot when pressure and angle allow.
First touch points the body toward the next pass.

commonMistakes.mistake: Receiver stands flat on the cone.
commonMistakes.correction: Check away, then return with one shoulder toward the next side.

commonMistakes.mistake: Receiver uses the near foot and closes the hips.
commonMistakes.correction: Let the ball travel to the far foot before cushioning.

commonMistakes.mistake: First touch stops under the body.
commonMistakes.correction: Guide it one step toward the next cone.

progressions.title: Two-touch rhythm
progressions.description: Use one touch to receive and one to pass.

progressions.title: Pressure cue
progressions.description: A passive defender points left or right, changing the safe receiving foot.

regressions.title: Shorter sides
regressions.description: Reduce each pass to eight yards.

regressions.title: Pause the picture
regressions.description: Stop after receiving so players can check body orientation.

steps.title: Build the diamond
steps.explanation: One player occupies each cone with the ball at the top.
steps.coachCue: See the ball and the next side.
steps.playerAction: Players prepare side-on at each cone.
steps.coachingPurpose: Make the next passing direction visible.

steps.title: Check away and arrive
steps.explanation: The right-side receiver moves away, scans, then returns as the passer looks up.
steps.playerAction: Receiver creates separation and returns side-on.
steps.ballAction: Passer holds until the receiver arrives.

steps.title: Receive toward the next side
steps.explanation: The receiver takes the ball across the body toward the bottom cone.
steps.coachCue: Across the body, into the next pass.
steps.playerAction: Receiver opens and guides the first touch clockwise.
steps.ballAction: Ball moves to the far foot and into useful space.
steps.coachingPurpose: Join body orientation to the next action.

steps.title: Pass and follow
steps.explanation: The receiver passes to the bottom cone while the original passer fills the right cone.
steps.coachCue: First touch out, pass on, follow quickly.
steps.playerAction: Receiver completes the next pass; passer follows.
steps.coachingPurpose: Create repeatable receiving rhythm and rotation.

safetyNotes: Place extra players behind, not beside, the starting cone.
Pause the pattern before retrieving a ball that enters another group's area.

payload.title: Purpose Box Retain
payload.summary: Shielders retain in a box against a live defender and must release to a target player within three seconds.
payload.description: An opposed box exercise where the shielder receives under pressure, holds with a stated purpose, and plays to a target on the sideline or turns away before the three-second count ends.

field.guidance: One 12-yard square per trio with a target on one sideline.

objectives: Shield side-on with body between ball and defender.
State and execute a purpose: release to target or turn away.
Connect within three seconds or lose possession.
setupInstructions: Mark a 12-yard square with a target cone on one sideline.
Shielder starts in center with ball; defender applies live pressure.
Target player moves along the sideline to create a passing angle.
Coach counts three seconds from first touch.
organization: Trios rotate shielder, defender, and target roles.
Multiple boxes for larger groups.
Shielder must call purpose before receiving the pass.
howItWorks: Target passes to shielder who receives under pressure.
Shielder holds with stated purpose while defender tries to win ball.
Within three seconds shielder passes to target or turns away successfully.
Failed retain or late release = defender becomes shielder.
resetInstructions: Restart from target pass after each attempt.
Uneven numbers use a coach as target or rotate waiting player.
coachingPoints: Receive already side-on when possible.
Ball on safe foot before pressure arrives.
Glance at target once during the hold.
Release firm and away from pressure.

commonMistakes.mistake: Shielder dribbles in circles without purpose.
commonMistakes.correction: Must call wait, turn, or release before the pass in.

commonMistakes.mistake: Target stands directly behind defender.
commonMistakes.correction: Target stays wide on the sideline.

commonMistakes.mistake: Defender fouls with hands.
commonMistakes.correction: Legal challenge only — coach resets on foul.

progressions.title: Two defenders
progressions.description: Add a second defender after three successful releases.

progressions.title: Turn-only purpose
progressions.description: Shielder must turn away — no pass option this round.

regressions.title: Passive defender
regressions.description: Defender jockeys without tackling for two rounds.

regressions.title: Five-second count
regressions.description: Extend time limit while learning body shape.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Quartets with rotating target; waiting player counts aloud.

steps.title: Box with target
steps.explanation: Shielder, defender, and sideline target set in a 12-yard square.
steps.playerAction: Shielder calls wait, turn, or release.
steps.ballAction: Ball with target to pass in.

steps.title: Receive under pressure
steps.explanation: Target passes in; shielder receives side-on as defender closes.
steps.playerAction: Shielder receives on safe foot.

steps.title: Hold with purpose
steps.explanation: Shielder drops hips and retains while glancing at target.
steps.playerAction: Shielder retains and scans target.
steps.ballAction: Ball on safe foot under pressure.

steps.title: Release to target, then rotate
steps.explanation: Shielder plays firm pass to target before count ends, then roles rotate.
steps.playerAction: Shielder releases to target.

safetyNotes: Legal challenges only in the box.
Target stays on sideline, not inside contest area.

payload.title: Escape Corridor
payload.summary: Attackers dribble through a corridor while a defender chooses one side to block; the attacker must turn away and escape.
payload.description: An opposed corridor exercise where the attacker approaches a live defender who can jockey but must stay on one side. The attacker scans, turns away from the block, and accelerates out of the corridor.

field.guidance: One 15-by-6-yard corridor per pair with a defender at the far end.

objectives: Scan before reaching the defender.
Turn away from the blocked side in one motion.
Accelerate out of the corridor within two touches.
setupInstructions: Mark a 15-by-6-yard corridor with cones.
Attacker starts at one end with a ball; defender waits at the far end.
Defender must choose left or right side before attacker enters last five yards.
Attacker scores by exiting the corridor under control within five seconds.
organization: Work 30-second rounds then swap roles.
Multiple corridors for larger groups.
Defender announces blocked side with a hand raise.
howItWorks: Attacker dribbles through the corridor at pace.
Defender shows which side is blocked before the attacker arrives.
Attacker scans, turns away from the block, and escapes.
Successful escape = exit under control; failed = defender touches ball.
Swap roles after each attempt.
resetInstructions: Restart from the corridor start after each attempt.
Waiting players rotate into defender role when numbers are uneven.
coachingPoints: Scan early — decide before the last five yards.
Turn away from the raised hand, not into it.
Protect with the body during the turn.
Explode on the escape touch.

commonMistakes.mistake: Attacker turns into the blocked side.
commonMistakes.correction: Defender holds the hand up until attacker commits correctly.

commonMistakes.mistake: Slow escape after the turn.
commonMistakes.correction: Time exits — under three seconds or restart.

commonMistakes.mistake: Defender blocks both sides.
commonMistakes.correction: Defender may only block one side per rep.

progressions.title: Live tackle
progressions.description: Defender can win the ball after the attacker enters the zone.

progressions.title: Reverse approach
progressions.description: Attacker starts facing away and receives before the corridor.

regressions.title: Passive block
regressions.description: Defender shows side but cannot move for three reps.

regressions.title: Wider corridor
regressions.description: Expand to eight yards wide.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Groups of three — third player calls blocked side from the sideline.

steps.title: Corridor and defender
steps.explanation: Attacker faces a narrow corridor with a defender at the far end.
steps.coachCue: Corridor clear — defender picks a side.
steps.playerAction: Attacker identifies corridor and defender.

steps.title: Approach with scan
steps.explanation: Attacker dribbles forward and checks over the shoulder.
steps.coachCue: Look before the last five yards.
steps.playerAction: Attacker scans while dribbling.
steps.coachingPurpose: Build scan timing before the turn.

steps.title: Defender blocks right
steps.explanation: Defender raises hand to block right; attacker turns left away from pressure.
steps.playerAction: Attacker turns left in one motion.

steps.title: Burst out, then swap roles
steps.explanation: Attacker accelerates out of the corridor before defender recovers, then partners reset and swap.
steps.playerAction: Attacker sprints out of corridor.

safetyNotes: Defender jockeys without reckless tackling in foundation rounds.
Keep corridors four yards apart.

payload.title: Available Ball at Home
payload.description: Practice surface switches and glance-up habits alone or with a partner, then reflect on when the ball felt free.
completionCriteria: Complete 30 surface switches using inside, outside, and sole on both feet.
Glance up after every third touch for at least 10 repetitions.
Answer one reflection question about when the ball felt free.
payload.easierOption: Walk through the lane slowly with a posted surface sequence and no time limit.
payload.harderOption: Jog the full sequence, add a passive partner shadow, and call free or tight aloud every five touches.
instructions: Set six cones in a line five steps apart in your yard or driveway.
Dribble through using inside, outside, and sole — alternate feet at each cone.
After every third touch, glance up and name one thing you see (space, wall, partner).
Repeat three times, then switch to your weaker foot leading.
Write or tell someone: when did the ball feel free versus tight?
Before your next practice, pick one reminder word: soft, close, or look.

payload.title: Find Three Open-Body Moments
payload.description: Practice the receiving shape at home, then identify where it could help in the next game.
instructions: Place two shoes three steps apart as a receiving gate and use a wall or partner.
Before each of 20 passes, check over one shoulder, open the hips, and receive across the body through either side of the gate.
Afterward, write or record one answer: what information helped you choose the receiving side?
Ask a parent or partner to watch five repetitions and identify when they could see both your chest and your next direction.
Before the next game, choose one personal reminder: scan early, open early, or first touch away from pressure.

payload.title: Shield with Purpose at Home
payload.description: Practice shield body shape alone or with a partner, name your purpose each hold, and reflect on when shielding helped you keep the ball.
completionCriteria: Complete eight shield holds of three seconds with correct body shape.
Name a purpose (wait, turn, or release) before each hold.
Successfully release with a pass or turn on at least six of eight holds.
payload.easierOption: Solo shield against a wall or cone with no pressure; focus on low hips and safe foot.
payload.harderOption: Partner applies shoulder pressure; release must reach a target cone five steps away within three seconds.
instructions: Stand side-on to an imaginary defender with the ball on your far foot.
Drop your hips, widen your base, and hold for three seconds.
Before each hold, say your purpose aloud: wait, turn, or release.
On release, pass to a wall, partner, or target cone — firm and away from pressure.
Repeat eight times, switching the foot you shield with every two reps.
Write or tell someone: when did shielding help you keep the ball today?

payload.title: Turn and Go at Home
payload.description: Practice one sharp turn and acceleration alone or with a partner, then note when a turn helped you escape pressure.
completionCriteria: Complete 10 turns on each foot with a glance up before every turn.
Accelerate within one stride after each turn for all repetitions.
Answer one reflection question about a turn that escaped pressure.
payload.easierOption: Walk through turns with a posted direction cone and no partner.
payload.harderOption: Add a partner who calls blocked side; race to a cone five yards away after each turn.
instructions: Place two cones eight steps apart as a mini corridor.
Dribble from one cone to the other, glance over your shoulder, and turn away in one motion.
Sprint back to the start cone — that is one rep.
Do five reps turning left, five turning right, then switch leading foot.
If a parent or partner is available, have them raise a hand for blocked side.
Write or say: when did a turn help you get away from someone?

objects.title: See the Next Play: Receive with an Open Body

payload.title: See the Next Play: Receive with an Open Body
payload.summary: Players learn to prepare side-on before the pass arrives, receive across the body, and keep both a forward option and a safe option visible.
payload.learningObjective: Prepare an open body shape before receiving so the first touch can support the best available next action.
successCriteria: The player scans before the pass travels or while it travels.
The player arrives side-on with hips able to see the passer and next space.
The player receives across the body when that touch protects a forward view.
The player can play forward or retain possession without first turning through pressure.
coachingPoints: Scan before receiving, then adjust the feet early.
Open the hips enough to see the ball and the next space.
Let the ball travel across the body when the far foot is safe.
Use the first touch to preserve two options, not to force forward play.

commonErrors.title: Closed body shape
commonErrors.description: The receiver faces only the passer, hiding the next space behind the body.
commonErrors.correction: Move one foot back and turn the hips before the ball arrives.

commonErrors.title: Receiving square
commonErrors.description: Both feet point at the passer, so the player needs an extra touch to turn.
commonErrors.correction: Arrive on a half-turn with one shoulder closer to the next action.

commonErrors.title: First touch into pressure
commonErrors.description: The receiver opens but pushes the ball toward the nearest defender.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the pressure first and choose the safe side of the body.

commonErrors.title: Watching only the ball
commonErrors.description: The receiver never checks the defender or next option before contact.
commonErrors.correction: Use a quick shoulder check before the pass, then return the eyes to the ball.

observableEvidence: Checks a shoulder before setting the receiving stance.
Receives side-on when pressure and the passing angle allow.
Uses the farther foot to let the ball travel across the body.
Keeps a forward and retaining option available after the first touch.
payload.progression: Move from unopposed body preparation to a live defender who changes the safe receiving side.
introduction: Ask players to show a closed shape, then turn one step so they can see the passer and a target ahead.
Explain that an open body does not mean always turning forward; it means seeing enough information to choose.

steps.title: Closed picture
steps.explanation: The receiver faces the passer squarely and cannot see the defender or forward target.
steps.playerAction: Receiver notices that the next space is behind the body.
steps.coachingPurpose: Make the cost of a square receiving shape visible.

steps.title: Scan and prepare
steps.explanation: Before the pass, the receiver checks the defender and opens one shoulder toward the next space.
steps.playerAction: Receiver scans and adjusts to a side-on stance.
steps.ballAction: Passer waits until the receiver is prepared.
steps.coachingPurpose: Connect scanning to early body preparation.

steps.title: Receive across the body
steps.explanation: The pass travels to the far foot so the receiver can cushion the ball toward the visible forward space.
steps.playerAction: Receiver cushions with the foot farther from the passer.
steps.ballAction: Ball travels across the body into the safe forward lane.
steps.coachingPurpose: Show how body shape and receiving foot work together.

steps.title: Choose the next action
steps.explanation: The receiver sees pressure and chooses either the forward target or the safe return pass.
steps.coachCue: Forward if open; keep it if closed.
steps.playerAction: Receiver selects from two visible options.
steps.ballAction: Ball stays playable on the safe side of the defender.
steps.coachingPurpose: Prevent open-body receiving from becoming a forced turn.

coachQuestions: What information should the receiver collect before the pass?
When would receiving across the body be unsafe?
Can the player still retain the ball after opening the body?
playerQuestions: Could you see both the ball and your next option?
Which foot kept the ball farthest from pressure?
What would tell you to play back instead of turning?

payload.title: Keep the Ball Available
payload.summary: Players learn to move the ball across different surfaces while keeping it playable, glancing up between touches, and noticing when the ball is free.
payload.learningObjective: Move the ball across both feet and the sole while keeping it within one stride and glancing up to notice nearby space.
successCriteria: The player changes surface without trapping the ball under the body.
The player glances up briefly between touches without losing control.
The player keeps the ball playable while walking or jogging.
The player can name when the ball is free versus when a defender is close.
coachingPoints: Soft touches keep the ball close enough to protect.
Use the sole to pause, then push to the safe foot.
Glance up between touches, not during contact.
Notice when the ball is free — that is the moment to look forward.

commonErrors.title: Heavy touches
commonErrors.description: The ball bounces too far and invites a tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Cushion with the inside of the foot and shorten the stride.

commonErrors.title: Head down the whole time
commonErrors.description: The player never sees teammates or pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Look at the ball on contact, then lift the eyes on the next step.

commonErrors.title: Only one foot
commonErrors.description: The player panics when the ball arrives on the weaker foot.
commonErrors.correction: Alternate surfaces deliberately in unopposed reps.

commonErrors.title: Standing on the ball
commonErrors.description: The player stops moving and loses forward options.
commonErrors.correction: Use the sole to settle, then push into motion within one second.

observableEvidence: Alternates inside, outside, and sole without stopping play.
Glances up between touches during movement.
Keeps the ball within one stride while changing direction.
Calls out or points when the ball is free.
payload.progression: Move from solo surface switches to a lightly opposed box where the player must keep the ball available under a passive shadow.
introduction: Ask players to dribble with their head down, then again with a glance up every two touches — which felt safer?
Explain that available means playable: close enough to protect, free enough to pass or turn.
Coach cue: Ball free? Eyes up. Ball tight? Protect first.

steps.title: Ball trapped underfoot
steps.explanation: The player stops on the ball with both feet square and cannot see forward.
steps.playerAction: Player notices the ball is trapped and vision is blocked.
steps.ballAction: Ball sits under the standing foot.
steps.coachingPurpose: Show the cost of stopping on the ball.

steps.title: Sole settle, push out
steps.explanation: The player uses the sole to pause, then pushes the ball to the inside of the safe foot.
steps.playerAction: Player settles with the sole and releases to the inside foot.
steps.ballAction: Ball moves from underfoot to a playable distance.
steps.coachingPurpose: Introduce sole as a reset, not a stop.

steps.title: Switch surfaces on the move
steps.explanation: The player moves forward using inside, outside, and sole while keeping the ball within one stride.
steps.playerAction: Player alternates surfaces while jogging.
steps.ballAction: Ball stays within one stride of the body.

steps.title: Glance up when free
steps.explanation: After two controlled touches, the player looks up and sees open space ahead.
steps.playerAction: Player glances up and identifies free space.
steps.ballAction: Ball remains playable during the scan.

coachQuestions: What tells you the ball is available versus trapped?
When is the sole useful instead of a big touch?
What did you see when you looked up?
playerQuestions: Could you keep the ball within one stride on both feet?
When did you notice the ball was free?
Which surface helped you change direction fastest?

payload.title: Shield with a Purpose
payload.summary: Players learn to use the body between the ball and the defender, retain possession with intention, and release the ball when support arrives or space opens.
payload.learningObjective: Place the body between the ball and pressure, keep the ball playable while shielding, and release to a teammate or into space when the purpose is clear.
successCriteria: The player gets side-on with the body between ball and defender.
The player keeps the ball within one stride while shielding.
The player can name why they are shielding — wait, turn, or release.
The player releases the ball within three seconds when support arrives.
coachingPoints: Low center of gravity — knees bent, arm legal and steady.
Ball on the safe foot, body on the pressure side.
Shield to keep, not to hide — eyes up for support.
Release when the purpose is achieved, not when panic arrives.

commonErrors.title: Standing tall
commonErrors.description: The player is upright and the defender reaches around.
commonErrors.correction: Drop the hips and widen the base.

commonErrors.title: Ball on pressure foot
commonErrors.description: The ball sits on the same side as the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Roll to the far foot and keep the body in between.

commonErrors.title: Shielding forever
commonErrors.description: The player holds the ball with no plan.
commonErrors.correction: Name the purpose: wait for support, turn, or play out.

commonErrors.title: Illegal holding
commonErrors.description: The player grabs or pushes the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Use the body position, not the hands.

observableEvidence: Gets side-on with body between ball and defender.
Keeps ball on the foot farther from pressure.
Glances up for support while shielding.
Releases with a pass or turn when support arrives.
payload.progression: Move from paired shield holds to a retain game where the shielder must connect within three seconds or turn away.
introduction: Ask: when is shielding useful — and when is it just hiding?
Shield with a purpose means you know what you are waiting for.
Coach cue: Body in, ball out — when the moment comes.

steps.title: Ball exposed
steps.explanation: The player faces the defender squarely with the ball in front — easy to poke.
steps.coachCue: Where is the ball relative to the body?
steps.playerAction: Player sees the ball is unprotected.
steps.ballAction: Ball sits in front of both feet.

steps.title: Side-on shield
steps.explanation: The player turns side-on with the body between ball and defender.
steps.playerAction: Player drops hips and shields with the body.
steps.ballAction: Ball moves to the far foot.

steps.title: Retain with purpose
steps.explanation: The player holds while glancing up for a teammate arriving wide.
steps.playerAction: Player shields and scans for support.
steps.ballAction: Ball stays playable on the safe foot.
steps.coachingPurpose: Connect shielding to a clear purpose.

steps.title: Release when ready
steps.explanation: Support arrives; the player rolls out and passes away from pressure.
steps.playerAction: Player releases to support.
steps.coachingPurpose: Complete the shield with intentional release.

coachQuestions: Why were you shielding in that moment?
How long is too long to hold?
When should you turn instead of passing?
playerQuestions: Was the ball on your safe foot?
Did you see support before you released?
What was your purpose — wait, turn, or play?

payload.title: Turn to Escape
payload.summary: Players learn to change direction with one sharp turn, accelerate away from pressure, and glance up before committing to the escape route.
payload.learningObjective: Scan before turning, use one decisive change of direction to escape pressure, and accelerate into open space within two touches.
successCriteria: The player glances up before choosing a turn direction.
The player completes the turn in one motion without multiple pivots.
The player accelerates immediately after the turn.
The player keeps the ball available through the turn.
coachingPoints: Know where pressure is before you turn.
One sharp turn beats three small shuffles.
First touch after the turn should explode into space.
Use the outside or inside based on which side is free.

commonErrors.title: Turning blind
commonErrors.description: The player spins without checking and runs into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Shoulder check, then turn away from the defender.

commonErrors.title: Multiple pivots
commonErrors.description: The player spins twice and loses the ball.
commonErrors.correction: Commit to one turn direction and protect with the body.

commonErrors.title: No acceleration
commonErrors.description: The player turns but jogs, letting pressure recover.
commonErrors.correction: Explode on the first touch after the turn.

commonErrors.title: Turn into traffic
commonErrors.description: The player turns toward teammates and defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Scan for the clearest lane before committing.

observableEvidence: Uses one decisive turn to change direction.
Accelerates within one stride after the turn.
Escapes pressure while keeping the ball within one stride.
payload.progression: Move from channel turns without pressure to a corridor game where a live defender chooses which side to block.
introduction: Show a slow spin versus one sharp turn — which got away from pressure faster?
Turn to escape means leave the defender behind, not just spin in place.

steps.title: Pressure behind
steps.explanation: The player faces forward with a defender approaching from behind.
steps.playerAction: Player feels pressure from behind.
steps.ballAction: Ball at player's feet facing forward.
steps.coachingPurpose: Establish the problem the turn solves.

steps.title: Shoulder check
steps.explanation: The player glances over the shoulder and sees pressure on the right.
steps.playerAction: Player scans and identifies pressure side.
steps.ballAction: Ball stays close during the scan.

steps.title: Turn away from pressure
steps.explanation: The player uses one sharp turn to the left, away from the defender.
steps.playerAction: Player turns left in one decisive move.
steps.ballAction: Ball stays within one stride through the turn.

steps.title: Accelerate into space
steps.explanation: The first touch after the turn explodes into the open lane.
steps.playerAction: Player accelerates into open space.
steps.ballAction: Ball pushes into the escape lane.
steps.coachingPurpose: Complete the escape with speed change.

coachQuestions: Which side was free before you turned?
How many touches did your turn take?

payload.title: Keep-Away Availability
payload.summary: Teams score by completing five consecutive available touches — ball within one stride with a glance up — before passing to a teammate.
payload.description: A directional keep-away game where possession teams earn a point when five touches stay available and include at least one look up. Defenders win the ball to attack the opposite goal.

field.guidance: 30-by-22-yard field with two small goals on end lines.

equipment: two mini goals or cone goals
objectives: Keep the ball available under light pressure in a game.
Glance up during possession before choosing a pass.
Notice when the ball is free and exploit the space.
setupInstructions: Mark a 30-by-22-yard field with mini goals on each end line.
Organize 4v4 or 5v5 with equal teams.
Possession team must complete five available touches before shooting.
Keep spare balls on both touchlines.
organization: Play 3-minute rounds with 1-minute coaching breaks.
Teams switch roles after each round.
Coach freezes only to highlight an available sequence.
howItWorks: The team in possession must keep the ball within one stride on each touch.
At least one player must glance up during the five-touch build-up.
After five available touches the team may pass into the goal or dribble through.
Defenders win the ball and immediately attack the opposite goal.
No points for a shot without five available touches.
resetInstructions: After a goal, restart with a pass from the scoring team's end line.
Use touchline spare balls when the ball leaves the field.
coachingPoints: Available touches are soft and close — not wild dribbles.
Look up on the step after contact.
When the ball is free, attack the space quickly.
Support players stay close enough to receive an available pass.

commonMistakes.mistake: Players chase the goal without five available touches.
commonMistakes.correction: Reset the count when a touch is too heavy.

commonMistakes.mistake: Head stays down through the whole sequence.
commonMistakes.correction: Require a visible look up before the scoring pass.

commonMistakes.mistake: Teammates stand too far to link available passes.
commonMistakes.correction: Support within 10 yards and at angles, not straight lines.

progressions.title: Three-touch maximum after build-up
progressions.description: After five available touches, finish within three team touches.

progressions.title: Bonus for weak foot
progressions.description: Two points if the scoring action uses the non-dominant foot.

regressions.title: Neutral floater
regressions.description: Add one neutral who always plays with possession.

regressions.title: Three-touch build-up
regressions.description: Reduce required available touches from five to three.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Play 4v3 with a neutral or rotate floater every two minutes.

steps.title: Two-goal keep-away
steps.explanation: Equal teams face opposite goals in a directional field.
steps.playerAction: Teams identify goals and possession rules.
steps.coachingPurpose: Create a game reason to keep the ball close.

steps.title: Build available touches
steps.explanation: Home links short passes keeping each touch within one stride.
steps.playerAction: Home maintains close possession.
steps.coachingPurpose: Reward playable distance in a game.

steps.title: Look up mid-sequence
steps.explanation: H2 glances up during the build-up and sees space to advance.
steps.coachCue: Look on the step after touch.
steps.playerAction: H2 scans and sees forward space.
steps.ballAction: Ball stays available during the scan.

steps.title: Ball free — attack
steps.explanation: After five available touches home plays forward into space.
steps.playerAction: Home exploits free ball moment.

steps.title: Turnover and transition
steps.explanation: Away wins the ball and attacks the opposite goal immediately.
steps.coachCue: Ball free for the other team — react.
steps.playerAction: Away transitions to attack.
steps.coachingPurpose: Plant the transition habit: notice when ball is free.

safetyNotes: Scale field to roster to avoid congestion.
Use mini goals without nets if space is tight.

payload.title: Open to Play Forward
payload.summary: A directional end-zone game that rewards receiving side-on and connecting forward without forcing the turn.
payload.description: A directional game in which teams score by finding a teammate arriving in an end zone. Bonus scoring rewards a prepared side-on reception followed by a controlled forward action, while safe retention remains a valid decision when pressure closes the route.

field.guidance: Use a four-yard end zone at each end; play 3v3 to 6v6 depending on roster.

objectives: Create a side-on receiving position between opponents.
Recognize when the first touch can go forward.
Retain possession when pressure closes the forward route.
setupInstructions: Mark a 30-by-22-yard field with a four-yard end zone at each end.
Organize equal teams from 3v3 to 6v6.
A team scores by completing a pass to a teammate arriving in the attacking end zone.
Keep spare balls on both touchlines for immediate restarts.
organization: Play equal teams from 3v3 to 6v6 in one directional field.
Teams attack opposite end zones and restart from their own end after a score.
Use short rounds with coaching between rounds rather than during live play.
howItWorks: Teams play directionally and may score only with a controlled reception in the end zone.
A reception that begins side-on and connects forward within two touches earns two points.
A normal controlled end-zone reception earns one point.
If the forward route is closed, retaining the ball remains live and is never penalized.
Coach interventions use brief freezes only when the receiver's preparation is clearly visible.
resetInstructions: After a score, the defending team restarts immediately from its end zone.
After the ball leaves the field, use the nearest spare ball and restart with a pass.
coachingPoints: Move outside the defender's cover shadow before asking for the ball.
Scan while the pass travels and adjust the receiving stance.
Open enough to see forward, but protect the safe return option.
First touch forward only when the space is genuinely available.

commonMistakes.mistake: Receiver waits in the end zone with a closed body.
commonMistakes.correction: Arrive from outside as the passer looks up.

commonMistakes.mistake: Players force a forward turn into pressure for the bonus.
commonMistakes.correction: Award the bonus only when the receiver keeps possession.

commonMistakes.mistake: Support stands directly behind a defender.
commonMistakes.correction: Move sideways until the passer can see both feet.

progressions.title: Midfield receiving bonus
progressions.description: Award one point when a player receives between defenders and connects forward within two touches.

progressions.title: Touch pressure
progressions.description: Use a three-touch maximum only after players consistently scan and prepare.

regressions.title: Neutral support
regressions.description: Add one neutral who plays with the team in possession.

regressions.title: Deeper end zones
regressions.description: Increase both end zones to six yards.

steps.title: Set two end zones
steps.explanation: Teams begin in a directional field with clear scoring zones.
steps.coachCue: Direction clear; arrive in the zone.
steps.playerAction: Teams spread and identify their attacking end zone.
steps.ballAction: Ball starts with the central home player.
steps.coachingPurpose: Create a directional reason to receive open.

steps.title: Create the receiving lane
steps.explanation: A wide player moves outside the defender's cover shadow and scans before the pass.
steps.coachCue: Out of the shadow; shoulder check.
steps.playerAction: H1 creates a visible diagonal lane and scans.
steps.ballAction: H2 protects the ball until the lane opens.
steps.coachingPurpose: Connect support movement to receiving orientation.

steps.title: Receive side-on
steps.explanation: The receiver opens to see the forward runner and the safe return pass.
steps.coachCue: Open hips; see forward and back.
steps.playerAction: H1 receives with both next actions visible.
steps.ballAction: Ball arrives on H1's safe foot.

steps.title: Play forward when open
steps.explanation: The receiver connects with a runner arriving in the end zone.
steps.playerAction: H3 arrives in the zone as H1 releases the pass.
steps.ballAction: Ball reaches the end-zone runner under control.
steps.coachingPurpose: Reward transfer from receiving shape to penetration.

steps.title: Retain when the route closes
steps.explanation: After a restart or turnover, the new receiver keeps the safe option instead of forcing forward.
steps.playerAction: Away retains through support because forward is blocked.
steps.ballAction: Ball moves safely away from immediate pressure.
steps.coachingPurpose: Protect decision quality from the scoring constraint.

safetyNotes: Maintain a clear buffer beyond both end lines.
Use touchline spare balls only after the previous ball is clearly out of play.
Scale field size to roster size to avoid repeated high-speed collisions.

payload.title: Retain to Connect
payload.summary: Possession teams score by shielding under pressure and connecting five passes within ten seconds.
payload.description: A keep-ball game where a player who receives under pressure must shield with a stated purpose before the team completes five passes. Turnovers happen when shielding exceeds three seconds without release or turn.

field.guidance: 28-by-22-yard field split into two equal zones optional.

objectives: Shield with a clear purpose when pressed in a game.
Release or turn within three seconds under live pressure.
Connect team passes after a successful retain.
setupInstructions: Mark a 28-by-22-yard field.
Organize 5v5 or 4v4 with one ball.
Team in possession must complete five passes to score a point.
Any player pressed must shield and release within three seconds.
organization: Play 3-minute rounds; highest pass chains wins.
Coach counts aloud when a shield begins.
Freeze briefly to highlight purposeful releases.
howItWorks: Teams keep possession in the field.
When a player is pressed, they must get side-on and shield.
Within three seconds they pass, turn away, or lose the ball.
Five consecutive team passes = one point.
Shielding without a visible purpose resets the pass count.
resetInstructions: Turnover restarts with the defending team in the center.
Use spare balls for out-of-bounds.
coachingPoints: Call your purpose when pressed — teammates adjust.
Support angles wide, not straight behind pressure.
Release firm; soft passes invite another press.
Turn away when no pass is on — that counts as release.

commonMistakes.mistake: Shielding until turnover without trying to release.
commonMistakes.correction: Coach counts three — turnover if no release.

commonMistakes.mistake: Teammates hide behind the presser.
commonMistakes.correction: Support must show outside shoulder of pressure.

commonMistakes.mistake: Illegal holding under pressure.
commonMistakes.correction: Reset and coach legal body position.

progressions.title: Two-touch after shield
progressions.description: After release, team must finish chain in two touches each.

progressions.title: Bonus for turn release
progressions.description: Two points if shield ends with a successful turn away.

regressions.title: Neutral overload
regressions.description: Add neutral who always plays with possession team.

regressions.title: Three-pass chain
regressions.description: Reduce required passes from five to three.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Play 4v3 with a neutral or rotate floater every goal.

steps.title: Keep-ball field
steps.explanation: Equal teams spread in a possession field.
steps.playerAction: Teams identify possession rules.
steps.coachingPurpose: Create game need for purposeful shielding.

steps.title: Press arrives
steps.explanation: H2 receives as A2 closes; must prepare to shield.
steps.playerAction: H2 gets body between ball and A2.

steps.title: Hold and scan
steps.explanation: H2 shields for two seconds and sees H1 wide.
steps.playerAction: H2 scans and finds H1.

steps.title: Release and chain
steps.explanation: H2 plays out to H1; team continues pass count.
steps.playerAction: H2 connects pass chain.

steps.title: Late shield turnover
steps.explanation: Away wins ball when shield exceeds three seconds without release.
steps.playerAction: Away wins possession.

safetyNotes: Coach enforces legal contact during shielding.
Scale field to avoid congestion.

payload.title: End-Zone Turn Game
payload.summary: Teams score by turning away from pressure in the attacking end zone and connecting a pass to a teammate.
payload.description: A directional small-sided game where players must enter the end zone, execute one turn away from pressure, and complete a pass to a teammate to score.

field.guidance: 32-by-24-yard field with a six-yard end zone at each end.

objectives: Turn away from pressure in the end zone under game conditions.
Accelerate after the turn to create a passing angle.
Connect with a teammate after the escape turn.
setupInstructions: Mark a 32-by-24-yard field with six-yard end zones.
Organize 4v4 or 5v5 equal teams.
Score by entering the end zone, one turn away from pressure, and completing a pass.
Keep spare balls on touchlines.
organization: Play 4-minute rounds with coaching between rounds.
Restart from defending end zone after scores.
Coach freezes to highlight clean escape turns.
howItWorks: Teams attack opposite end zones directionally.
A player with the ball must enter the end zone under control.
Inside the zone the player must turn away from the nearest defender once.
Score requires a completed pass to a teammate after the turn.
Turning into pressure or multiple pivots resets the attack.
resetInstructions: Defending team restarts from their end zone after a score.
Use spare balls for out-of-bounds restarts.
coachingPoints: Enter the zone under control — not at full sprint.
Scan before the turn inside the zone.
Accelerate after the turn to open the passing lane.
Support runners arrive at angles, not straight lines.

commonMistakes.mistake: Player turns before entering the zone.
commonMistakes.correction: Turn only counts inside the shaded end zone.

commonMistakes.mistake: Multiple spins in the zone.
commonMistakes.correction: One turn rule — reset if broken.

commonMistakes.mistake: Teammates stand behind defenders.
commonMistakes.correction: Support from wide angles outside the zone.

progressions.title: Two-touch finish
progressions.description: Pass after turn must happen within two touches.

progressions.title: Weak-foot turn bonus
progressions.description: Two points for escape turn on non-dominant foot.

regressions.title: Deeper end zones
regressions.description: Expand end zones to eight yards.

regressions.title: Unopposed turn first
regressions.description: Defenders wait outside zone for two rounds.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Play 4v3 with a neutral attacker in the end zone.

steps.title: End zones marked
steps.explanation: Teams face opposite six-yard end zones in a directional field.
steps.playerAction: Teams identify end zones and scoring rule.
steps.coachingPurpose: Create game context for escape turns.

steps.title: Drive into the zone
steps.explanation: H1 dribbles toward the attacking end zone with a defender closing.
steps.playerAction: H1 approaches zone with ball available.

steps.title: Turn away in the zone
steps.explanation: H1 scans and turns left away from A1 inside the end zone.
steps.playerAction: H1 executes single escape turn.

steps.title: Pass after escape
steps.explanation: H1 accelerates and finds H2 after the turn.
steps.playerAction: H1 passes to H2 after acceleration.

steps.title: Defenders counter
steps.explanation: After turnover away turns and attacks opposite zone.
steps.playerAction: Away transitions to attack.
steps.coachingPurpose: Reinforce transition habit from lesson one.

safetyNotes: End zones should not overlap with touchline hazards.
Scale field for roster size.

payload.title: Surface Switch Lane
payload.summary: Players move through a cone lane switching inside, outside, and sole touches while glancing up at each gate.
payload.description: An individual or paired warmup that builds comfort changing surfaces on the move. Each gate prompts a called surface so players cannot rely on one foot or one touch pattern.

field.guidance: One 25-yard lane per pair with a cone gate every five yards.

equipment: one ball per player or pair
objectives: Switch inside, outside, and sole without stopping.
Glance up at each gate while keeping the ball close.
Keep the ball within one stride through the lane.
setupInstructions: Mark a 25-by-12-yard lane with cones every five yards.
Place one player per lane or pairs sharing one ball.
Coach calls the surface at each gate: inside, outside, or sole.
Leave three yards between parallel lanes.
organization: Players dribble down the lane and return jogging.
Alternate starting foot each repetition.
Run 60-second rounds with 20-second resets.
howItWorks: The player dribbles toward the first gate on the coach's called surface.
At each gate the player glances up, then performs the next called touch.
At the end the player turns and returns using the opposite surfaces.
Partners alternate if sharing one ball.
resetInstructions: Retrieve loose balls from the side of the lane before restarting.
Rotate starting positions if numbers are uneven.
coachingPoints: Soft touches — the ball should not outrun the player.
Glance up at the gate, not at the coach.
Use the sole only to settle, then push forward.
Both feet must appear in every round.

commonMistakes.mistake: Big touches into the next lane.
commonMistakes.correction: Shorten touches and widen lane spacing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Player watches the coach instead of scanning forward.
commonMistakes.correction: Point to the gate as the look-up target.

commonMistakes.mistake: Only using the dominant foot.
commonMistakes.correction: Require the weaker foot at two gates per rep.

progressions.title: Partner mirror
progressions.description: Pairs call surfaces to each other instead of the coach.

progressions.title: Speed change
progressions.description: Jog the lane, then sprint the return with the same control.

regressions.title: Known sequence
regressions.description: Post the surface order on a cone before each rep.

regressions.title: Wider lane
regressions.description: Expand to 15 yards wide and slow to walking pace.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Run individual lanes with shared balls; extra players become gate callers.

steps.title: Set the lane
steps.explanation: Cones mark gates every five yards with space to turn at the end.
steps.playerAction: Player identifies gate spacing and turn zone.
steps.ballAction: Ball starts at the player's feet.

steps.title: Inside through gate one
steps.explanation: The player uses the inside of the foot and glances up at the first gate.
steps.playerAction: Player glances at the gate while cushioning inside.
steps.coachingPurpose: Pair surface work with early scanning.

steps.title: Outside at gate two
steps.explanation: The coach calls outside; the player shifts the ball to the other foot.
steps.playerAction: Player changes foot without breaking stride.

steps.title: Sole settle at gate three
steps.explanation: The player pauses on the sole, glances up, then pushes forward.
steps.playerAction: Player uses sole to settle then releases.
steps.coachingPurpose: Teach sole as a control surface, not a trap.

steps.title: Turn and return
steps.explanation: The player turns at the end and returns with the opposite foot leading.
steps.playerAction: Player turns and switches leading foot.
steps.ballAction: Ball stays close through the turn.

safetyNotes: Keep three yards between parallel lanes.
Players turn away from neighbors at the end line.

payload.title: Open-Body Gate Check
payload.summary: Pairs pass through a gate while the receiver scans, opens, and takes the first touch toward a called exit.
payload.description: A continuous partner warmup that introduces scanning and open-body receiving without opposition. The passer supplies a late directional cue so the receiver must prepare early, control the ball through a safe exit, and reset quickly.

field.guidance: Use one four-yard gate per pair with six yards behind each side.

objectives: Scan before the partner passes.
Prepare a side-on stance outside the gate.
Receive across the body toward the called exit.
setupInstructions: Create one four-yard cone gate per pair.
Place partners six yards apart on opposite sides with one ball.
Name the two exit directions behind each receiver.
Leave at least three yards between neighboring pairs.
organization: Work in pairs with one active ball and one gate.
Both players alternate passer and receiver roles after every repetition.
Run 60-second rounds with a short reset between rounds.
howItWorks: The receiver checks both exits before the pass.
The passer calls left or right as the ball travels.
The receiver opens, takes the ball through the gate toward that exit, then passes back from the new angle.
Partners alternate receiving roles continuously.
resetInstructions: If the ball leaves the area, the nearest player retrieves it while the partner restores the gate position.
Switch the starting passer after each 60-second round.
coachingPoints: Scan before the pass starts.
Move the feet early; do not wait for the ball to fix the body shape.
Use the foot farther from the passer when it keeps the exit visible.
Cushion the first touch within one stride.

commonMistakes.mistake: Receiver waits square inside the gate.
commonMistakes.correction: Start just outside and arrive side-on as the pass travels.

commonMistakes.mistake: Player turns before controlling the ball.
commonMistakes.correction: Watch the final part of the pass and cushion before accelerating.

commonMistakes.mistake: First touch crosses into the neighboring pair.
commonMistakes.correction: Shorten the touch and enlarge spacing between gates.

progressions.title: Late visual cue
progressions.description: The passer points to an exit instead of calling it.

progressions.title: Two-touch return
progressions.description: Receive through the exit and return the pass in two touches.

regressions.title: Known exit
regressions.description: Choose the receiving direction before the pass.

regressions.title: Wider gate
regressions.description: Increase the gate to six yards and shorten the pass.

steps.title: Set the gate
steps.explanation: Partners begin opposite a clear gate with space behind both exits.
steps.playerAction: Receiver starts outside the gate and scans both directions.
steps.ballAction: Ball begins under the passer's control.
steps.coachingPurpose: Establish safe spacing and two possible exits.

steps.title: Open before the pass
steps.explanation: The receiver checks over the shoulder and turns the hips toward the called exit.
steps.playerAction: Receiver adjusts the feet before the ball travels.
steps.ballAction: Passer prepares a firm ground pass.

steps.title: Receive through the exit
steps.explanation: The receiver uses the far foot and guides the first touch through the selected side.
steps.playerAction: Receiver cushions into the called lane.
steps.ballAction: Ball crosses the body and exits under control.
steps.coachingPurpose: Coordinate body shape, foot choice, and first touch.

steps.title: Pass back and change roles
steps.explanation: The receiver turns to face the partner, returns the ball, and becomes the next passer.
steps.playerAction: Partners exchange passer and receiver roles.

safetyNotes: Keep at least three yards between neighboring gates.
Players retrieve loose balls only after checking adjacent working lanes.

payload.title: Pair Shield Hold
payload.summary: Partners take turns shielding for three seconds while the other applies light shoulder pressure, then release with a pass.
payload.description: A paired warmup that teaches low body shape and safe foot placement. The shielder must call their purpose — wait, turn, or release — before the hold begins.

field.guidance: One eight-yard circle or square per pair.

objectives: Get side-on with body between ball and partner pressure.
Keep the ball on the safe foot for three seconds.
Release with a firm pass when the coach calls release.
setupInstructions: Pair players with one ball in an eight-yard square.
Shielder starts with ball; partner applies light shoulder pressure.
Shielder calls purpose: wait, turn, or release before each hold.
Coach counts three seconds then calls release.
organization: 30-second work rounds then swap roles.
Partners stay in the same square for four rounds.
Rotate pairs if numbers are uneven.
howItWorks: Shielder gets side-on and holds for three seconds.
Partner applies legal shoulder pressure without tackling.
On release call, shielder plays a pass to the partner.
Partners swap shielder and pressure roles each round.
resetInstructions: Loose balls restart from the center of the square.
Extra players wait behind squares and rotate in.
coachingPoints: Low hips, wide base, legal arms.
Ball on the foot farther from pressure.
Eyes up once during the hold.
Release decisively — no extra dribbles.

commonMistakes.mistake: Partner pushes with hands.
commonMistakes.correction: Shoulder pressure only — hands behind back.

commonMistakes.mistake: Shielder stands upright.
commonMistakes.correction: Coach freezes and resets until hips drop.

commonMistakes.mistake: Holding past the release call.
commonMistakes.correction: Count aloud — release on three.

progressions.title: Named support
progressions.description: Third player becomes support; release must find them.

progressions.title: Turn release
progressions.description: Shielder turns away instead of passing on release.

regressions.title: No pressure
regressions.description: Solo shield hold against a cone as imaginary defender.

regressions.title: Longer hold
regressions.description: Extend to five seconds for body shape focus only.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Trios with two shielders alternating; third calls purpose and counts.

steps.title: Pair square
steps.explanation: Shielder and partner face each other in an eight-yard square.
steps.playerAction: Shielder names wait, turn, or release.

steps.title: Side-on shape
steps.explanation: Shielder drops hips and places body between ball and partner.
steps.playerAction: Shielder gets side-on with ball on safe foot.

steps.title: Hold for three
steps.explanation: Partner applies shoulder pressure; shielder retains for three seconds.
steps.playerAction: Shielder retains and scans once.

steps.title: Release on call
steps.explanation: Coach calls release; shielder passes firmly to partner.
steps.playerAction: Shielder plays out to partner.

steps.title: Swap roles
steps.explanation: Former presser becomes shielder for the next round.
steps.playerAction: Partners swap roles.

safetyNotes: Shoulder pressure only — no pushing with hands.
Keep squares four yards apart.

payload.title: Channel Turn Relay
payload.summary: Players dribble through narrow channels, execute one turn at the end, and sprint back using the opposite foot.
payload.description: A relay warmup in parallel channels that isolates one sharp turn at each end. Players must glance up before turning and accelerate on the return leg.

field.guidance: One 20-by-8-yard channel per player with a turn zone at each end.

objectives: Execute one sharp turn at each end of the channel.
Glance up before committing to the turn direction.
Accelerate immediately on the return leg.
setupInstructions: Mark parallel 20-by-8-yard channels four yards apart.
Place one player with a ball at the start of each channel.
Define a two-yard turn zone at each end with cones.
Coach calls inside or outside turn at each end.
organization: Players dribble down, turn once, and return.
Alternate turn direction each repetition.
Run 45-second relays with 15-second resets.
howItWorks: The player dribbles through the channel at jogging pace.
At the turn zone the player glances up and executes one called turn.
The player accelerates back using the opposite foot to lead.
Next player starts when the previous player crosses the start line.
resetInstructions: Loose balls are retrieved from the side without crossing neighbors.
Odd numbers create one resting channel — rotate every round.
coachingPoints: One turn — not three small steps.
Look at the open side before the turn.
Explode on the first touch after turning.
Keep the ball close through the turn.

commonMistakes.mistake: Multiple pivots in the turn zone.
commonMistakes.correction: Shrink turn zone and require exit within two touches.

commonMistakes.mistake: Jogging the return leg.
commonMistakes.correction: Time the return — beat your previous sprint.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning without looking.
commonMistakes.correction: Freeze players who turn before a visible shoulder check.

progressions.title: Weak-foot turns
progressions.description: Every turn must use the non-dominant foot.

progressions.title: Partner race
progressions.description: Side-by-side channels — first clean turn wins.

regressions.title: Wider channel
regressions.description: Expand to 12 yards wide and walk the approach.

regressions.title: Known turn side
regressions.description: Post turn direction on a cone before each rep.

regressions.title: Uneven attendance
regressions.description: Share channels in pairs — one dribbles, one calls turn direction.

steps.title: Parallel channels
steps.explanation: Each player has a narrow channel with a turn zone at the far end.
steps.coachCue: One channel each — turn at the end.
steps.playerAction: Player identifies channel boundaries.

steps.title: Dribble to turn zone
steps.explanation: The player jogs forward keeping the ball available.
steps.playerAction: Player dribbles toward turn zone.

steps.title: One sharp turn
steps.explanation: At the end the player checks over the shoulder and turns away in one motion.
steps.playerAction: Player executes single decisive turn.
steps.ballAction: Ball stays close through the turn.

steps.title: Sprint the return
steps.explanation: The first touch after the turn explodes back toward the start.
steps.playerAction: Player sprints return leg.

steps.title: Tag the next player
steps.explanation: Returning player high-fives the next starter at the line.
steps.playerAction: Next player starts immediately.

safetyNotes: Keep four yards between parallel channels.
Players turn away from neighbors at each end.
